headline: Scalable tools for mapping activity landscapes and benchmarking screening in large chemical spaces
label: Chemical Space Navigation Methods
summary: New methods for library-scale clustering, bias-reduced benchmarks and automated consensus screening address the growing size of accessible chemical space.
synthesis: The common thread is computational navigation of large compound collections, together with the evaluation of screening methods used on them. BitBIRCH clustering locates activity cliffs or smooth regions in large libraries, and a substituent network built from same-target co-occurrence in literature data maps bioisosteric replacements. Work on expanding academic ultralarge virtual libraries addresses the exploration of billions of compounds. New in this set is the emphasis on screening infrastructure and benchmark quality: VS-Suite automates consensus screening by combining Boltz-2 co-folding with AutoDock Vina and GNINA docking, and MolSCISSOR resplits LIT-PCBA into SPLIT-PCBA to reduce structural and physicochemical bias. The items differ in method and validation design, so they reflect a shared orientation rather than a uniform finding.
